newsitem.title: UK: Camelot pledges to work with next UK govt.
newsitem.headline: Camelot pledges to work with next UK govt.

text.p: UK national lottery operator Camelot said on Wednesday it would work with the next government, regardless of which party forms it.
"We're happy to work with the government of the day and will continue to operate the national lottery in accordance with parliament's wishes," a Camelot spokeswoman said.
The opposition Labour Party had earlier restated its intention to replace Camelot with a "competitive, efficient, not-for-profit operator" when its licence ends in 2001.
Labour national heritage spokesman Jack Cunningham said Camelot should not be able to retain millions of pounds of interest on undistributed prize money.
The Camelot spokeswoman said the consortium was currently in discussions with lottery regulator Oflot about this issue.

Labour is proposing a one billion stg fund for education and health projects from the proceeds of thr new midweek draw. The Camelot spokeswoman pointed out that the distribution of funds was not the company's responsibility.
